lead.hed: Ronald Reagan ran flight operations in the Pacific on Oct. 11
lead.insight: DVIDS posted a Navy photograph of sailors on the flight deck of USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76) in the Pacific Ocean on Oct. 11. The caption says the Nimitz-class carrier is underway conducting routine training in the U.S. 3rd Fleet area of operations. The photograph was taken by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Hannah Kantner and posted Oct. 12.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Hannah Kantner · DVIDS 10007314 · Public domain · Sailors take part in flight operations on the flight deck of USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76) in the Pacific Ocean. Photo taken Oct. 11, 2026.

political.hed: A Manila speech on deterring China drew little coverage
political.insight: Wednesday's Heritage commentary says media focus on the war in Iran left Undersecretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby's speech in Manila with little coverage. The piece says that gap means few people know what the United States and its allies are doing to deter China from launching hostilities of its own.

political.hed: History and tradition does not require a matching old practice
political.insight: Tuesday's Law & Liberty essay says the Supreme Court has never required a long, unbroken history of one specific government act before that act can pass the Establishment Clause. Mark David Hall recalls Marsh v. Chambers, where the Court upheld legislative chaplains because the practice was deeply embedded from the founding. He says some advocates in recent Ten Commandments school cases treat the absence of an identical classroom posting as decisive. The Court, he writes, has upheld practices of more recent origin even when Lemon was still the test.

tech.hed: Army generals want larger, more frequent drills in Korea
tech.insight: Defense News reported Wednesday that Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of United Nations Command, Combined Forces Command, and United States Forces Korea, told the Association of the United States Army meeting he wants exercises that are more frequent and spread across the peninsula. He said the two big annual drills still center on large command posts, and that Ukraine argues for training in a distributed way, from Jeju Island to Gyeonggi Province. Lt. Gen. Joe Hilbert, commander of Eighth Army, said an August order scaled back one exercise, Ulchi Freedom Shield, cutting its live portion in half. He said joint training with South Korea otherwise continues, including 2nd Infantry Division troops on South Korean ranges.

tech.hed: Forterra put its autonomy software on a Hypercraft ground vehicle
tech.insight: Defense News reported Wednesday that Forterra and Hypercraft showed an autonomous ground vehicle at the Association of the United States Army exposition in Washington. Forterra installed its AutoDrive software on Hypercraft's Razorback. Chief Growth Officer Scott Sanders said the point of an autonomous military vehicle is to deliver payloads to the point of friction. The company said AutoDrive is already on more than 200 vehicles in service. In August the Army named Forterra a prime contractor for the Engineer Autonomous Breaching Capability program.

culture.hed: A First Things review separates the online right from the religious right
culture.insight: Aaron M. Renn's Wednesday review of Scott Greer's Whitepill says Greer, a former editor at Richard Spencer's Radix Journal, treats Trump's appeal as identity rather than the economic story in Hillbilly Elegy and American Compass. Renn writes that Greer ties American identity to white identity, a claim the older conservative movement denied under the creedal-nation idea. The review is the desk's culture item for the evening board.
